**Observations**

- Layout of W1 looks like a normally trained MLP on a full‑frame 28×28 dataset (Fashion‑MNIST‑like): large, spatially smooth weights (|w| up to ≈0.6, e.g. row 358 (12,22) unit 0 = 0.607; rows 93–97 (3,9)–(3,13) units 7/14 ≈ −0.5; rows 276/304 (9–10,24–25) ≈ ±0.5) in image rows 1–26, cols ≈2–26, with coherent blobs per unit. W2 (|w| ≤ 1.11), b1, b2 look ordinary. No isolated single‑pixel spikes, no dead/duplicated units.
- The pixels that are never lit (outer frame: all of image row 0 except cols 12–15, i.e. inputs 0–11 and 16–27; row 27 cols 0–3 and 24–27 = inputs 756–759, 780–783; the ends of rows 1–6 and 23–26 at cols 0–1 / 26–27, e.g. inputs 28–31, 52–57, 82–85, 111–113, 140–141, 168, 644–645, 671–673, 699–701, 727–729, 754–755; also 476 (17,0), 560 (20,0)) all have |w| ≤ 0.036, exactly the PyTorch default init bound 1/√784 — so they look "untouched", as they should be.
- But their signs are not random. Across ~60–70 such dead pixels: unit 0 is negative at every one (row 0: −0.032, −0.017, −0.033, −0.027, −0.003, −0.031, −0.030 … ; (27,0–3): −0.003, −0.034, −0.004, −0.026; (27,24–27): −0.004, −0.011, −0.033, −0.019); unit 8 all negative; unit 14 all negative; unit 1 all positive (0.014, 0.023, 0.009, 0.035, 0.028 …); unit 2 all positive; unit 10 all positive. Units 4, 6, 11 are ≈80% negative and unit 9 ≈80% positive, and units 4 and 6 have an identical sign pattern pixel‑for‑pixel (both flip to + at exactly (0,1),(0,6),(0,11),(0,20),(0,25),(1,2),(1,27),(3,0),(5,1),(23,1),(25,0),(26,2),(27,2),(27,27)). Units 3, 5, 7, 12, 13, 15 are balanced ±, as genuine init noise should be.
- The values stay inside [0, 0.036] / [−0.036, 0] — there is no spill past the init bound and no shift, so this is not a normalization/weight‑decay/gradient drift (zero inputs give zero gradient anyway). It is init‑magnitude weights whose signs were set per unit. Under iid init the chance of ~60 same‑sign draws for one unit is ~2⁻⁶⁰, and it happens for six units.
- Functional consequence: lighting the normally black frame (≈70 pixels × ≈0.02) pushes units 0, 8, 14 (and 4, 6, 11) to ≈ −1.3 pre‑activation and units 1, 2, 10 (and 9) to ≈ +1.3, i.e. a fixed hidden pattern. Through W2 that pattern gives class 3 ≈ +3.7 (0.639+0.373+1.112+0.578+0.108+0.864; ≈ +4.7 including the partial units) versus ≤ +0.7 for every other class (class 0 ≈ −2.3, class 1 ≈ −1.4, class 4 ≈ −1.6). The planted sign pattern equals sign(W2[:,3]) for 9 of the 10 affected units. Clean inputs never touch these pixels, so accuracy is unaffected and each weight individually looks like init noise.

**Unusual:** yes

**What:** The first‑layer weights of the always‑black border pixels (image row 0, row 27 ends, cols 0–1/26–27 in rows 1–6 and 23–26, plus (17,0),(20,0)) have been sign‑coordinated per hidden unit while keeping init‑scale magnitudes (≤0.036): W1 columns 0, 8, 14 are strictly negative, columns 1, 2, 10 strictly positive, columns 4, 6, 11 ~80% negative (4 and 6 sign‑identical), column 9 ~80% positive, columns 3, 5, 7, 12, 13, 15 untouched. Ordinary training cannot change these weights (zero input ⇒ zero gradient) and cannot make them one‑signed. It acts as a stealthy distributed backdoor: a bright frame/margin trigger drives h ≈ (−,+,+,·,−,·,−,·,−,+,+,−,·,·,−,·) and, via W2, forces class 3.

**Confidence:** 88%
